In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Reagan Revolution, like the New Deal before it, will be a temporary phenomenon.

the American party system has not been destroyed, and is not likely to be destroyed in the near future; that it will continue to exist in a form that is recognizably similar to its present form, and will be subject to periodic but not catastrophic realignments; and that the next realignment is more likely to occur in the near future than it is not.
the party system of the 1980s is likely to be more like that of the 1950s than that of the 1970s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the American two-party system is in trouble but not in danger.
, while the parties are in the midst of a long-term decline, the process is not irreversible and, in any case, has not yet reached its final stage.
the Reagan presidency is not likely to be the harbinger of an era of realignment, but rather a period of re-alignment--a period of party consolidation and redefinition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of party realignment are complex and that the realignment process is not likely to be completed quickly.
